3

The big idea

Four methods in v2, one function in v3

Commands v2

initialize() runs once, at the start.

execute() is called by the scheduler every 20 ms.

isFinished() is checked every loop.

end(interrupted) runs once, at the end.

Commands v3

One function runs top to bottom, like normal Java.

coroutine.yield() pauses until the next 20 ms loop.

Reaching the end, or return, finishes the command.

whenExited(...) holds cleanup that runs however it ends.

4

Writing a v3 command

A v3 command reads in the order the robot acts

Feeder.java

  /** Right: whenExited runs however the command ends. */

  public Command intake() {

1   return run(coroutine -> {

1         motor.setThrottle(FEED_SPEED);

2         coroutine.waitUntil(this::hasPiece);

        })

3       .whenExited(() -> motor.setThrottle(0.0))

4       .named("Intake");

  }

1

run(...)

Requires this mechanism. setThrottle is 2027’s set.

2

Wait for a sensor

Yields every loop until it is true.

3

Cleanup

Runs however the command ends.

4

A name is required

No name, no command: it won’t compile.

6

Common mistake

run means something different

What you see

A drive command copied from v2 moves for one loop, then stops. The command ends at once.

Why it happens

v2’s run calls its code every 20 ms. v3’s run calls its function once, and a function with no loop ends right away.

The fix

Use runRepeatedly where v2 used run, or write the loop yourself with coroutine.yield().

run(() -> drive.arcadeDrive(f, r))           // v2: every 20 ms

run(c -> drive.arcadeDrive(f, r))            // v3: once, then ends

runRepeatedly(() -> drive.arcadeDrive(f, r)) // v3: every 20 ms

Deck 13 · Commands in 2027

7

Writing a v3 command

Deck 2’s drive, as a mechanism

KitBotDrive.java

/** Drive from the sticks. Lowest priority, so any other command can take over. */

public Command arcadeDrive(DoubleSupplier fwd, DoubleSupplier rot) {

  return runRepeatedly(() -> drive.arcadeDrive(fwd.getAsDouble(), rot.getAsDouble()))

      .withPriority(Command.LOWEST_PRIORITY)

      .named("Arcade Drive");

}

runRepeatedly is v2’s run. The lowest priority lets any other command take the drive.

Deck 13 · Commands in 2027

8

Priorities

Priorities replace “interruptible or not”

When a new command conflicts with a running oneWhat happens
The new one has a higher priorityIt starts. The old one is cancelled.
They have the same priorityIt starts. The old one is cancelled.
The new one has a lower priorityIt is discarded. The old one keeps running.

The default priority is 0. Command.LOWEST_PRIORITY suits default commands and idles.

Deck 2, in v2

The routine students already wrote

deck2/DriveAutos.java

/** The same routine as a list: easier to read, reorder and extend. */

public static Command leaveAndTurn(CANDriveSubsystem drive) {

  return Commands.sequence(

          drive.driveArcade(() -> AUTO_SPEED, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(DRIVE_OUT_SECONDS),

          drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> 0.0).withTimeout(PAUSE_SECONDS),

          drive.driveArcade(() -> 0.0, () -> AUTO_SPEED).withTimeout(TURN_SECONDS),

          Commands.print("Auto finished"))

      .withName("Leave and turn");

}

Deck 2’s code, unchanged: it compiles against WPILib 2026.

11

v3, builder

The same routine with v3’s builder

DriveAutos.java

/** The builder: closest to Deck 2's Commands.sequence. */

public static Command leaveAndTurn(KitBotDrive drive) {

  return Command.sequence(

          drive.driveFor(AUTO_SPEED, 0.0, DRIVE_OUT),

          drive.idleFor(PAUSE),

          drive.driveFor(0.0, AUTO_SPEED, TURN))

      .named("Leave and Turn");

}

idleFor holds still because KitBotDrive makes its idle drive at zero. The name ends the builder.

Deck 13 · Commands in 2027

12

v3, coroutine

The same routine as plain steps

DriveAutos.java

/** The coroutine: plain Java, one step after another. */

public static Command leaveAndTurnSteps(KitBotDrive drive) {

  return Command.requiring(drive)

      .executing(coroutine -> {

        coroutine.await(drive.driveFor(AUTO_SPEED, 0.0, DRIVE_OUT));

        coroutine.await(drive.idleFor(PAUSE));

        coroutine.await(drive.driveFor(0.0, AUTO_SPEED, TURN));

        System.out.println("Auto finished");

      })

      .named("Leave and Turn (steps)");

}

await starts a command and waits for it to end. Any Java fits between steps.

Sequences

Combining commands in v3

Write thisIt runsIt ends when
Command.sequence(a, b).named(...)each one in orderthe last one ends
coroutine.await(a)a, and this waitsa ends
Command.parallel(a, b).named(...)a and b at onceboth have ended
Command.race(a, b).named(...)a and b at onceeither one ends
Command.parallel(a).optional(b)a and b at oncea ends, and b is cancelled
coroutine.fork(a)a in the backgroundthis keeps going
a.withTimeout(Seconds.of(2))a for at most 2 secondsa ends or the time is up

14

Common mistake

The roller keeps spinning after a cancel

What you see

Bound with whileTrue, the feeder keeps running after the driver lets go of the button.

Why it happens

Cancelling stops the function where it is, inside waitUntil. The line that stops the motor never runs.

The fix

Put stop code in whenExited, which runs however the command ends, as on the first command slide.

motor.setThrottle(FEED_SPEED);

coroutine.waitUntil(this::hasPiece); // cancelled while waiting here

motor.setThrottle(0.0);              // so this never runs

Deck 13 · Commands in 2027

15

Best practice

Every loop yields

Put coroutine.yield(), or a wait that yields, in every loop in a command.

A loop that never yields freezes the whole robot. WPILib’s compiler plugin turns a while loop with no yield into a build error.

while (!atTarget()) { drive.arcadeDrive(0.4, 0); }   // build error

 

while (!atTarget()) {

  drive.arcadeDrive(0.4, 0);

  coroutine.yield();                                 // one loop at a time

}

16

Control theory

A feedback loop that reads like the math

Arm.java

  public Command holdAt(double target) {

    return run(coroutine -> {

1         pid.reset();

          while (true) {

2           double now = angle.getAsDouble();

2           double ff = KG * Math.cos(now); // gravity

3           motor.setVoltage(ff + pid.calculate(now, target));

4           coroutine.yield(); // one 20 ms step

          }

        })

        .whenExited(() -> motor.setVoltage(0.0))

        .named("Arm Hold");

  }

1

Reset

A fresh start for each run.

2

Measure, then feedforward

Gravity, from Deck 6.

3

Feedback

P on the angle error.

4

One sample

Each yield is one 20 ms step: the loop’s dt.

Scopes

Bindings and default commands now have a scope

Made inLasts until
The Robot constructorThe robot code stops
autonomousInit, by schedulingAutonomous ends: the auto is cancelled
An OpModeThat OpMode ends
A running commandThat command ends

When a scope ends, its trigger bindings are removed and its default commands are put back.

18

The robot class

Deck 2’s bindings and chooser, in v3

Robot.java

public Robot() {

  drive.setDefaultCommand(

      drive.arcadeDrive(

          () -> -MathUtil.applyDeadband(driver.getLeftY(), DEADBAND) * DRIVE_SCALE,

          () -> -MathUtil.applyDeadband(driver.getRightX(), DEADBAND) * TURN_SCALE));

 

  driver.faceDown().onTrue(feeder.intake());

 

  autoChooser.addDefault("Leave and Turn", DriveAutos.leaveAndTurn(drive));

  autoChooser.add("Leave and Turn (steps)", DriveAutos.leaveAndTurnSteps(drive));

  Tunables.publish("Auto", autoChooser);

}

robotPeriodic calls Scheduler.getDefault().run(). autonomousInit schedules the chosen auto.

Deck 13 · Commands in 2027

19

Best practice

Default commands get the lowest priority

Give every default command Command.LOWEST_PRIORITY. Raise the priority only for a command that must not be stopped.

A default command’s priority is the lowest that can ever take its mechanism. Set it high, and button commands are discarded.

20

Choosing

v2 or v3 for your team in 2027

Stay on v2

Same as these decks: only package names change.

Every language: C++ and Python have only v2.

Known patterns: years of examples and team code.

Try v3

Reads like Java: loops, ifs and waits, in order.

Safer by default: required names, yield checks, priorities.

New in 2027: alpha now, so check your libraries support it.

Recap

What this deck covered

WPILib 2027 keeps v2 and adds v3, which is for Java only.

A v3 command is one function: loops yield, return ends it.

runRepeatedly is v2’s run. v3’s run runs its function once.

Names are required, and stop code goes in whenExited.

Priorities, scopes and await replace interrupt flags and proxies.
